editorial.headline: Soil and Clay Extraction With a Clear Bali PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the extraction and basic processing of soil and clay, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is for the practical business of taking soil and clay out of the ground, then preparing those materials through forming, crushing, or grinding. Its scope is not a vague construction catch-all. It is anchored in excavation and in the first physical handling of soil and clay materials after extraction. The record names the output universe clearly: kaolin or china clay, ball clay or firing clay, abu bumi, shale, and fill soil. That makes the activity relevant to operators dealing in raw or prepared earth materials, rather than businesses further downstream in finished goods.

The registration window is broad. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the same classification can serve a small local operator as well as a larger excavation business. The record also notes Permohonan IPR Koperasi and Permohonan SIPB, which signals that the activity sits close to formal resource-use administration. Those items should be read exactly as stated: they appear in the activity scope, but the record does not give thresholds, timelines, issuing procedures, or documentary requirements. A founder should therefore treat them as part of the activity’s regulatory context, not as permission to infer a complete licensing checklist.

Seen from Jakarta's rulebook, foreign investment in this activity raises no flags. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership shown in the record is 100%. In plain English, the activity is open to foreign ownership at the national level, with no foreign-share cap shown in this slim record. The source given for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company assessing whether the activity can sit inside an Indonesian investment structure, that is the central national answer: the classification itself is not closed to PMA, and the record gives a full foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali is often where the nuance appears, but here the record does not show a moratorium block. The province’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. This activity, however, is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest Bali reading is therefore not “nationally open but locally blocked.” It is nationally open, and on this record it remains available for PMA registration in Bali, while still carrying the higher-risk administrative character indicated by the Bali status note.
